letter.subject: Complaint regarding cookie and tracking practices on prudentialplc.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns about cookie and tracking activity observed on https://prudentialplc.com during an automated, passive audit on 2026-11-08 04:08 UTC. The audit used a fresh browser, clicked the cookie banner’s reject option (“Decline”), and recorded what was still stored or sent while browsing https://www.prudentialplc.com/zh-hant/, https://www.prudentialplc.com/zh-cn/, and https://www.prudentialplc.com/en/investors/overview/. I also reviewed your privacy notice at https://www.prudentialplc.com/en/site-services/privacy-notice/.

Please explain the following points:

1. Our review suggests there is a conflict between observed advertising-related data sharing and the statement in your privacy notice that, “We use this information only to analyse the use of our website to help guide improvements.” Before the banner was answered, the unique _ga identifier was sent to doubleclick.net, which the audit identifies as Google advertising. This appears inconsistent with the stated purpose.

2. Two Google cookies, _ga and _ga_TGBX5LZFVH, were already set before any choice was made on the cookie banner. These cookies held what appears to be a unique identifier.

3. After the reject option was clicked, 10 requests were still made to googletagmanager.com.

4. Before the cookie banner was answered, the value of _ga, appearing to be an identifier unique to this browser, was sent to doubleclick.net and google.co.uk in the request address. This appears capable of allowing Google to recognise the browser on later visits.

In light of the above, please:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking technologies from being set, accessed, or used without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker

ai_review.summary: The audit found Google identifiers and advertising-related requests before the user answered the banner and after rejection, as recorded in the automated checks. In addition, the policy says cookie information is used only for website analysis, which conflicts with the observed advertising-related sharing. The privacy notice covers several UK GDPR transparency items, but does not clearly describe this advertising disclosure or provide a specific cookie-policy explanation.
